name: Alinma Capital
legal_name: Alinma Capital Company (a Saudi Closed Joint Stock Company); formerly Alinma Investment Company
founded: 2009 (ministerial resolution 183 dated 31 May 2009; CR 1010269764 dated 16 Jun 2009; CMA licence 09134-37 dated 19 Apr 2009; operations began 17 Jan 2010). Renamed from Alinma Investment Company to Alinma Capital (CMA notice 12 Feb 2025).
ownership_summary: Wholly owned by Alinma Bank (50,000,000 shares, 100%; no change during 2025). Authorised capital SAR 1bn; paid-up capital SAR 500m.
government_link: Indirect. The parent, Alinma Bank, is 10% owned by the Public Investment Fund (see sa-alinma).
group_structure: 100% subsidiary of Alinma Bank (sa-alinma). Consolidates Alinma Private Equity Opportunities Fund (72.92%, established 4 Jul 2023). Also sets up special-purpose companies to hold assets of its real estate and private equity funds; these are not consolidated (AR 2025). Double counting: Alinma Capital is fully consolidated into Alinma Bank and drives the bank's 'Investment and brokerage' segment. The segment is close to but not identical to Alinma Capital's standalone accounts (FY2025 segment total operating income SAR 1,128.5m vs Alinma Capital total income SAR 1,091.0m). Never add this record's figures to sa-alinma.

subsidiaries.name: Alinma Private Equity Opportunities Fund
subsidiaries.activity: Closed-ended private equity fund (direct and fund investments, KSA and abroad)

footprint: Saudi Arabia. 6 branches listed on the website (checked 12 Oct 2026): Riyadh HQ (Al Anoud Tower 2), Altakhassusi, Al-Ghadeer and Al Rabwah in Riyadh; Alhada in Al Khobar; Ash Shati in Jeddah. Also distributes through Alinma Bank. International brokerage covers GCC, Egypt, US, Europe and Asia-Pacific markets.
customer_segments: Individual investors (retail and HNW, including Alinma Bank affluent and Private Banking clients, who get discounts on Alinma Capital products); families (private family funds); corporates and institutions (investment banking, custody, mandates); endowments and non-profits (endowment funds).
business_lines: Asset management: public funds, Sukuk ETF, REIT, endowment funds, private funds. Alternative investments: real estate and private equity funds. Discretionary private portfolios and investment mandates. Wealth management and investment advisory. Brokerage: Saudi and international, with Murabaha margin facilities. Investment banking: ECM, DCM, M&A, underwriting. Custody. FY2025 revenue (SAR '000): asset management fees 543,153; brokerage commission 44,474; investment banking fees 42,339; Murabaha and Wakala services 37,434; custody fees 17,239; other 5,584; margin lending income 85,824. 554,384 of the 776,047 revenue came from related parties (mainly funds it manages).

capabilities.wealth_summary: Alinma Capital (renamed from Alinma Investment in Feb 2025) is Alinma Bank's 100%-owned, Shariah-only CMA licensee for dealing, managing, arranging, advising and custody. AUM was SAR 104.6bn at end-2025 and SAR 129.7bn at 30 Jun 2026; the parent calls it the 3rd-largest asset manager in KSA by AUM. The book is dominated by alternatives: more than SAR 84bn in 44 real estate and private equity funds, against about SAR 15bn in private portfolios/mandates and about SAR 5.4bn in 20 capital-markets, money-market and fixed-income funds (72 funds in total). FY2025 revenue was SAR 776m, of which asset management fees were SAR 543m and brokerage commission SAR 44.5m. 71% of revenue came from related parties. Brokerage covers Tadawul plus GCC, Egypt, US (including fractional shares), European and Asian markets through the Alinma Capital app and web platform and a separate 'Alinma Capital Global' platform. In 2025 it launched a new website and app experience and an in-house investment-allocation tool called 'Nasih'. Its 2030 strategy targets partnerships with global asset managers to co-develop funds, a top-tier wealth advisory team, a new engagement-led brokerage app and an AI-powered wealth companion.

private_banking.detail: Private banking is run by the parent bank's Private Banking Group (see sa-alinma). Alinma Capital provides wealth management, private portfolios and private family funds to those and other clients.

asset_management.detail: 72 funds at end-2025. Public funds listed on the website: Alinma Nomu Market Equity, Free-Style Saudi Equity, Emerging Markets Equity, Diversified Saudi Riyal, Saudi Equity, IPO, Multi-Assets Balanced (monthly distribution), Saudi Riyal Liquidity, plus Alinma Saudi Government Sukuk ETF. Also private funds, REITs (e.g. Alinma Hospitality REIT), endowment funds (AUM SAR 402m) and private family funds. 13 new private funds in 2025 (+SAR 7.6bn AUM). New private fund with SAR 447mn AUM in 2Q26. Five Sanadeq awards for 2025 fund performance.

brokerage.detail: Local (Saudi Exchange) at 0.155% of traded value. International: Dubai, Abu Dhabi, Nasdaq Dubai, Kuwait, Bahrain, Qatar, Muscat, Egypt, USA (per-share pricing, fractional shares), London and other European markets, Australia, NZ, China, Hong Kong, Japan, Singapore and other Asian markets. The site says it 'cooperates with major prestigious brokerage companies'. Channels: branches, phone brokers, IVR trading, web and app. Murabaha share-trading facilities (margin; board raised the limit to SAR 2bn in 2025); Shariah purification service; technical analysis; live prices. 2026 plans: institutional trading desks and market-making.

digital_investing.detail: 'Alinma Capital' app (iOS seller: Alinma Investment Company; v3.0.44): buy/sell orders, IPO subscriptions, Sukuk orders, mutual fund subscription and redemption, portfolio analysis. Web platform 'Alinma Capital Platform' (online.alinmacapital.com) for the local market. 'Alinma Capital Global Platform' and app for international markets. New main website and unified app/web experience launched 2025. Alinma Bank customers also reach in-house funds through the bank app's wealth platform (see sa-alinma).

advisory.detail: CMA licence covers advising. 'Investment Management Advisory' service is built on an Investment Policy Statement. Wealth Management team promises 'best advisory practice through the optimal allocation of investment assets' across local and global opportunities. 2030 plan: 'Set up a top-tier wealth advisory team'.

discretionary.detail: Private investment portfolios managed by Alinma Capital's team to the client's objectives and Shariah rules, with a dedicated relationship manager and performance reporting. Private portfolios and investment mandates AUM about SAR 15bn at end-2025 (+16%).

model_portfolios_robo.detail: No client-facing robo-advisor or model-portfolio product found. In 2025 IT 'developed and launched the "Nasih" (ناصح) solution to support investment allocation' based on analysis of client data, risk level and interactive responses. It is unclear whether clients use it directly or advisers use it internally. Parent's 2030 plan includes an 'AI-powered wealth companion'.

funds_platform.detail: Distributes its own funds through app, web, branches and the parent bank. No third-party fund shelf or fund-platform provider found.

structured_products.detail: No structured products on the Alinma Capital website or app listing. The parent bank lists structured products for alinma Private clients (see sa-alinma).

private_markets.detail: Core franchise: alternatives AUM above SAR 84bn at end-2025 (44 funds). Real estate (residential, commercial, industrial, hospitality, Makkah/Madinah, logistics), private equity funds (including the consolidated Alinma Private Equity Opportunities Fund, 72.92%), and private real estate and public/traded real estate funds. Forbes ME 2026 cites 2025 private real estate funds in Dammam (USD 5.1bn), Jeddah (USD 4.7bn) and Makkah (USD 2.3bn).

islamic_wealth.detail: All activities Shariah-compliant under its own Sharia Committee: Sukuk ETF, Murabaha and Sukuk funds, Shariah share-purification service, Murabaha margin facilities, endowment (waqf) funds.

partners.what: The official site's 'Global Market' login points to alinmainternational.globaltradingnetwork.com, and its Google Play link for the Alinma Capital app uses package ID com.gtn.alin. This suggests GTN provides the trading platform technology. No announcement found; the relationship is inferred from official links.

initiatives.what: CMA announced the company's name change from Alinma Investment to Alinma Capital, with a new visual identity
Launched 13 new private funds (real estate, energy, healthcare, financing, Murabaha, fixed income), adding SAR 7.6bn AUM. Executed 18 IB transactions.

Digital and IT: new main website, unified app/web UX, trading and margin/IPO/sukuk/fund journey upgrades, 'Nasih' investment-allocation tool, T24 integration, portfolio and wealth management system automation integrated with CRM
Board approved the company's 2030 strategy and raised the margin financing limit to SAR 2bn

Outlook (parent AR 2025): scale investment solutions for individual and institutional segments; set up institutional trading desks and market-making; broaden global reach; AI/GenAI-enabled operating model. Plans to add new markets to the global trading platform and improve e-channels for account opening and trading (Alinma Capital AR).

Parent's 2Q26 strategy update for Alinma Capital: 9 of 13 initiatives started. Focus areas include partnering with global AMs to co-develop funds, a top-tier wealth advisory team, local and global distribution, a new app with engagement features, and an AI-powered wealth companion. Launched a new private fund with SAR 447mn AUM.

opportunities: 2030 focus areas include 'Forge partnerships with global AMs to co-develop funds', 'Set up local and global distribution in key markets', 'Launch cutting-edge app with engagement features and modules' and 'Enhance CX with AI-powered wealth companion and personalization' (S7 slide 18)
Liquid public-market fund range is small next to alternatives: about SAR 5.4bn in 20 capital-markets/money-market/fixed-income funds vs more than SAR 84bn alternatives (S5 pp.9, 14)
No model portfolios, robo product, third-party funds or structured products found on the website or app listing (S16, S17)
Brokerage revenue is shrinking: brokerage commission fell from SAR 64.2m (FY2024) to SAR 44.5m (FY2025) (S4 note 19.1), and H1 2026 brokerage trading income fell 20% YoY (S7 slide 47)
Plans to add markets to its global trading platform and improve digital account opening and trading (S5 p.28)
barriers: Shariah-only: products need Sharia Committee approval (S3)
In-house build culture: developed the 'Nasih' allocation tool internally in 2025 and runs T24, a GTN-hosted global platform and its own apps (S5, S16)
Captive model: 71% of FY2025 revenue (SAR 554m of SAR 776m) from related parties, mainly its own funds (S4 note 19.1)
Large proprietary alternatives franchise (SAR 84bn+) limits the need for third-party private-markets products (S5)
incumbent_vendors: Global Trading Network (GTN): inferred from the globaltradingnetwork.com-hosted global platform login and com.gtn.alin Android app ID on the official site (S16)
T24 core system, named in AR 2025 (S5)
